title: NBA2 — queue additions from the independent cross-check (session arena/5b80b88a-nba2)
source_note: Merge-ready fragment. These rows are NOT applied to suggestions/SUGGESTIONS.json or requirements/QUESTIONS.json by this session, because those files feed data/site.json and the generated pages that session arena/79e87c81-nba2 is rebuilding on PR #21; editing them here would have meant editing shared outputs someone else had claimed. An integration session appends the objects below verbatim and rebuilds — the field names match the existing schemas exactly, so no other change is needed. Every row is derived from a check in analysis/crosscheck-5b80b88a.md, which is generated by tools/crosscheck_site.py.

suggestions.title: Run the cross-check in CI, next to the lint
suggestions.problem: The provenance lint proves rows are labelled; the CI parity step proves the HTML equals a rebuild of site.json. Neither can prove a label matches what it points at, because the same code produced both. Three audits said the same thing: nobody had re-run a semantic pass over the published values. tools/crosscheck_site.py now does that, and it found six real defects on its first run.
suggestions.proposal: Add one CI step: `python3 tools/crosscheck_site.py --json crosscheck.json`, failing only on the checks the owner has accepted as binding (the tool exits non-zero on any FAIL, so start it as `continue-on-error: true` and promote it once the six findings are resolved).
suggestions.benefit: The class of defect that has recurred here — a count in prose drifting from the data underneath it — becomes impossible to ship silently.
suggestions.risk: Fails the build on cosmetic prose drift until the allow-list is set; that is the point, but it will annoy whoever merges at 23:00.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept after the six current findings are fixed, so it starts green.

suggestions.title: Render the two parlay sections that are built but never published
suggestions.problem: `build_site_data.py:852-853` produces `parlays_xg` (cross-game parlays, 2 rows) and `parlay_costs` (stacking cost arithmetic, 5 rows). `build_site.py:260` puts only `correlation` and `parlays` on pages/parlays.html. The rows count toward the lint, the row totals, and CI parity, but appear on no page — 7 published rows nobody can review, including the cross-game and cost analysis the brief explicitly asks for.
suggestions.proposal: Append `render_table(sec("parlays_xg"), L), render_table(sec("parlay_costs"), L)` to the pages/parlays.html list and rebuild. Note the deliberate `legs = (1,2,3,4,6)` skip in `build_cost_rows` is intentional, not a dropped row — checked, not assumed.
suggestions.benefit: Two analysis tables become visible; the row-count claim on the landing page stops being larger than what a reader can actually open.
suggestions.risk: None. The data is already linted and parity-checked; only its rendering is missing.

suggestions.title: Make the 'W-L (official NBA.com)' column an actual official measurement
suggestions.problem: `build_ratings_rows` (build_site_data.py:111) fills both `wl` and `wl_official` from the same model object, which is loaded from the Basketball-Reference snapshot. The table's own note says 'Both W-L columns are printed on purpose: if they ever disagree, the table is wrong' — a guard that cannot fire, because the two columns are the same number by construction. Meanwhile the real official capture (`nba2/data/records.json`, read from nba.com) is not compared in the row at all, and the coverage caveat ('28 of 30 clubs visible in the retrieved page text, TOR and WAS not') lives only in the table caption, never per row.
suggestions.proposal: Populate `wl_official` from `nba2/data/records.json` keyed by the normalised tricode, flag the two rows whose official confirmation came from a *different* official page (TOR/WAS via their team pages), and keep the caption as the summary it is.
suggestions.benefit: The column earns its label; the disagreement guard becomes real; a reviewer sees per club which official document covered it, which is exactly what the 28/30-vs-30/30 confusion was missing.
suggestions.risk: If a row then disagrees, the table shows a FAIL for that club — which is the desired behaviour, not a regression.

suggestions.title: Stop reporting AT-RISK gates as 'blocked' on the leaderboard
suggestions.problem: `leaderboard.py:149` computes `blocked = sum(result in ('BLOCKED','AT-RISK'))`, so all nine strategies publish '0 pass / 0 fail / 10 blocked' while the gate matrix underneath them says 8 BLOCKED + 2 AT-RISK. The gates page defines the two states differently ('BLOCKED means the input does not exist; AT-RISK means the input exists but the measurement is at risk'), and the distinction is the roadmap: AT-RISK gates are the ones a single data change can move.
suggestions.proposal: Add `gates_at_risk` to the tally and publish '0 pass / 0 fail / 8 blocked / 2 at-risk', or split the column in two.
suggestions.benefit: The leaderboard tells you which gate is closest to passing instead of flattening two very different states into one word.
suggestions.risk: Changes one rendered string and its test expectations.

suggestions.title: Normalise team keys at ingest, before any automation is written
suggestions.problem: `originated/data/teams.json` keys Washington as `WSH`; every other committed capture uses `WAS`. A join on tricode does not fail — it silently drops the club, which is precisely how a coverage figure like '28 of 30' can be read as a data defect when it is a keying artefact. The cross-check only found it because it counted coverage separately from agreement.
suggestions.proposal: One canonical alias table (`TRICODE_ALIAS`) in `nba2/provenance.py` applied to every ingest path and every cross-surface comparison, plus a test that fails if any committed surface introduces a key outside the canonical 30.
suggestions.benefit: Every future cross-source comparison — odds, injuries, player feeds — stops losing rows invisibly.
suggestions.risk: Renames nothing; only comparisons change. Legacy surfaces keep their own keys.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept, and do it before the ingestion workflow is promoted from probe to publish.

suggestions.title: Retire or re-earn FLAG-RAT-02
suggestions.problem: The ratings snapshot's `internal_consistency_checks` publishes two FAILs: 'sum(close_w) == sum(close_l) (FAIL)' and the same for blowout games, and FLAG-RAT-02 repeats it on the site as an extraction defect, which is why those four columns are excluded from every model input. Recomputing the sums from the same file's own 30 records gives 99 = 99 and 88 = 88 — balanced. The flag describes a defect the committed data does not contain.
suggestions.proposal: Either re-read the source page and show where the imbalance lives (the snapshot as committed is then not the file that was checked, which is its own problem), or update the labels to PASS, retire FLAG-RAT-02 and un-exclude the close/blowout columns for the luck and fatigue factors that want them.
suggestions.benefit: A false alarm stops costing two usable columns, and the site stops publishing a self-accusation it cannot substantiate.
suggestions.effort: low (documentation) / medium (if the columns come back into the model)
suggestions.risk: Un-excluding columns changes model inputs, so it must ride with a re-seal of the ledger, not a quiet rebuild.
suggestions.recommendation: Decide the label first, the inputs second.

suggestions.title: Stop hand-copying counts into prose
suggestions.problem: `README.md:82` still says '(49 tests)' while line 62 says 55 and the suite runs 55. Every earlier session hit some variant of this: counts written by hand, then drift. The numbers a reader most wants to trust — rows, tables, pages, tests — are the ones nobody re-measures.
suggestions.proposal: Generate the README's count block from the same measurement the cross-check uses (`CC-DOC-01` measures all four), or replace the inline numbers with a pointer to the sources page and its retrieval stamps.
suggestions.benefit: Removes the single most repeated documentation defect in this repository, permanently.

suggestions.title: Show staleness as a state, not a footnote
suggestions.problem: The site prints its snapshot date honestly, and every audit has had to say the same sentence in different words: the deployment succeeding does not mean the data is fresh. A reader skimming the picks page sees a line for a game that may already have tipped. Nothing on the page changes colour when the snapshot ages.
suggestions.proposal: Client-side only (so CI parity is untouched): `app.js` reads the published `snapshot_as_of`, compares with the browser date, and prints a banner — 'snapshot N days old; games on these dates have already tipped; nothing here is a live price' — with the freshness rule quoted from the sources page. Suppress the banner inside the repo's own checks by keying it to the data attribute rather than a build timestamp.
suggestions.benefit: The one mistake this prototype can cause in the real world — someone betting off a stale page — gets a stop sign at the top of every page.
suggestions.risk: Must not read the clock at build time or the byte-stability guarantee breaks.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept; it is the cheapest decision-safety change available.

suggestions.title: Keep the ingestion workflow as a probe until the runner evidence says otherwise
suggestions.problem: The official endpoints are unreachable from the sandbox that assembled this data, which is why so many columns are blank. The new workflow measures whether a GitHub-hosted runner sees the same thing. Until that measurement is read, 'we could not fetch' and 'nobody can fetch' are different plans with the same current output.
suggestions.proposal: Run `nba-ingest.yml` (dispatch, capture off) from main; record the run id and the endpoint table on the sources page. If nothing answers, delete the schedule trigger and say so in the requirements register: ingestion then needs a licensed feed or a human-verified capture, not a cron job.
suggestions.benefit: Turns the project's biggest open assumption into a dated, citable measurement.
suggestions.risk: A nightly job that always fails is noise; that is why the schedule stays off until the probe result is known.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept the measurement; defer the schedule.

questions.question: Which execution environment can reach the official NBA endpoints, and under what policy?
questions.have: A dated, reproducible measurement from the sandbox: four endpoints, none answering at TLS. Plus the same result from three prior sessions. The `nba-ingest.yml` probe measures it from a GitHub-hosted runner and prints the table.
questions.missing: The runner's answer (recorded by the probe run), and the owner's decision about whether automated fetching of nba.com properties is in policy for this project at any cadence.
questions.how: Dispatch the probe from main; read the run summary; if reachable, confirm terms of use before enabling a schedule; if unreachable, mark ingestion 'blocked by source policy' in the requirements register instead of 'not started'.
questions.impact: Decides whether the daily-refresh requirement is an engineering task, a licensing task, or a manual one. Nothing downstream (CLV, settled ledger, promoted strategies) can start without it.

questions.question: Is the 13:00 ET referee PDF the authority for availability, and do we keep the bytes?
questions.have: Three different stamps of the same day's report are cited across surfaces (01:00 PM, 04:15 PM, 05:15 PM ET) and the reconciliation table already adjudicates 10 status changes between them. The capture tool archives the PDF with a sha256 of the response body.
questions.missing: A policy: which stamp is canonical for a published line, and whether archived PDFs (or only their hashes) are kept in-repo.
questions.how: Owner picks 'latest release before tip, with the previous two retained'; then the ingest stores the PDF, its hash, and its stamp with every snapshot.
questions.impact: Without a canonical stamp, two honest sessions will keep disagreeing about who is Out, and the disagreement will look like a model difference.

questions.question: Which surface is canonical, and what happens to the other four?
questions.have: The root generated site (index.html + pages/**, 33 tables / 915 rows) is the Pages landing; `docs/`, `dashboard/`, `originated/`, `verified/` and the legacy root pages are all still published, each with its own model, window and injury conventions, and each with a passing checker of its own.
questions.missing: An owner decision: retire, archive under a clear label, or keep as alternates — plus a rule for what a new session may write into (because right now a new session adds a sixth surface by default).
questions.how: Pick one; move the others to `archive/` with a redirect note on each landing, or keep them and put the surface inventory (already a published table) at the top of the landing page.
questions.impact: Five surfaces means five answers to 'what is our line for DEN@NOP', all defensible, none canonical. That is the failure mode a leaderboard project cannot afford.

questions.question: What does a strategy have to survive before it can be paid?
questions.have: Nine gates per strategy defined and applied to 9 strategies (90 gate results, all BLOCKED/AT-RISK); a pre-registered sealed ledger (22 predictions, digest on every page); a tier ladder with reward weights; and a stated minimum sample of 300 settled bets.
questions.missing: Owner sign-off on the promotion rule as a *policy*, not a design: minimum sample, holdout window, vig treatment, drawdown cap, multiple-comparison correction across nine strategies, and what happens to the seal when the window rolls forward daily.
questions.how: Write it into the requirements register as acceptance criteria, then let the gate code enforce it; anything not enforced is a poster.
questions.impact: Until this exists, 'top performing strategies' has no definition, so the competition cannot start — and the honest answer today is that the leaderboard is empty by design.
